source.text: Mend.io has proactively upgraded 184 open source organizations and GitHub users to the Mend Renovate Community (OSS) plan, with no request required. At a glance The Community (OSS) plan is a tier of Mend Renovate Cloud, the Mend-hosted version of the Renovate dependency update tool, built for open source maintainers. It gives projects higher resource limits and increased concurrency, so they can keep dependencies up to date without hitting operational bottlenecks. The plan also unlocks Merge Confidence, which is currently only available on the Enterprise plan. Merge Confidence analyzes real-world adoption and test data across the Mend Renovate early-adopter ecosystem to flag releases that may introduce undeclared breaking changes. Together, these features reduce the burden on maintainers and make it easier to keep their software up to date and secure. source.text: Tensorlake provides isolated sandboxes for running untrusted, LLM-generated code, with checkpointing, suspend, and resume capabilities. Its npm SDK lets developers create and manage those environments from TypeScript applications. source.text: Starting today, AWS Lambda durable functions increases the maximum number of durable operations per execution from 3,000 to 30,000, and the maximum checkpoint payload size from 256 KB to 1 MB. Higher operation limits let you safely do more work in a single execution including expanding iterative loops, polling for longer time periods, and building more complex rollback paths that run when a step fails. source.title: This Shit is Hard: Building a vulnerability database from private reports
source.text: A finding against one release does not answer those questions for everyone using other versions of the package. Athena brings together vulnerability findings from across the industry so coalition members can coordinate remediation, mitigations, and disclosure. Most of these findings arrive before a public advisory or upstream fix exists. To date, Athena has validated 21,175 zero-day vulnerabilities. Turning those findings into information that guides remediation requires understanding which defect each report describes, where it exists, and what has already been done to address it. Consider two reports about the same package. One describes a vulnerability in an older release; the other describes similar behavior in the latest version but points to a different function. They could be separate vulnerabilities, or two paths to the same one. An upstream change may already fix one release line while leaving another affected. source.title: Hackers hijacked 1,900 GitHub accounts. Then they went after 30,000 repos.
source.text: Hackers accessed roughly 1,900 GitHub accounts, then used them to slip credential-stealing workflows into more than 30,000 repositories. The malicious GitHub Actions jobs targeted CI/CD secrets, cloud access keys, and AI provider API keys. GitGuardian tracked the GhostAction campaign as it intensified, with the biggest push on October 8 and 9, when the attackers reached repositories belonging to about 3,000 users and organizations and tried to extract 3,174 secrets. The tj-actions/changed-files compromise poisoned a shared Action used by thousands of repositories. GhostAction took a different route, using stolen developer credentials to modify workflows directly, with no vulnerability in GitHub Actions itself. It’s unclear how the attackers obtained those credentials, but StepSecurity’s October 9 analysis points to personal access tokens pulled from credential dumps as the likely source, though the initial compromise hasn’t been confirmed. With access to the repositories, the attackers could then add disguised workflows of standard security jobs, while using names like security-audit.yml or github_actions_security.yml.
